references.text: God reveals his name as 'I am' (Ehyeh) and emphasizes that he is the first and the last, without beginning or end, which mirrors Jesus' claim to be 'I am' before Abraham came into being.
The Lord declares that he is the first and the last, and that there is no god besides him, a direct parallel to Jesus' use of the absolute 'I am' to demonstrate his divine identity.
God says: 'Hear me, Jacob and Israel, my called one: I am he, I am the first, I am also the last,' which emphasizes eternity and self-existence that Jesus also claims in relation to Abraham.
God reveals his name as 'I am who I am' (Ehyeh asher ehyeh) to Moses, a name that Jesus uses directly in John 8:58 to identify himself with the eternal God.
The Word was in the beginning, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God, which establishes Jesus' existence before the beginning of time, consistent with the claim to be before Abraham.
Jesus asks to be restored to the glory he had with the Father before the world existed, confirming his existence before Abraham's time and emphasizing his eternal nature.
